scope: Targeted metadata workflow: CB_NULL transport lifecycle, CREATE_SESSION channel limits, SMB notification revocation cleanup and SMB3 cipher-free negotiation. Does not cover the later CB_SEQUENCE/retry changes or full SMB/NFS conformance.

checks: CREATE_SESSION binds a bidirectional transport; CB_NULL uses the requested program/version and AUTH_NONE while forechannel RPC stays usable
probe replies are bound to their exact TCP connection and XID; cross-connection, duplicate and unknown replies cannot change path state
BACKCHANNEL_CTL changes program and invalidates old probes; malformed matched replies keep path down and idempotent rebinding reprobes it
cleared callback credentials and destroyed/recreated sessions cannot be validated by a stale probe response
BIND_CONN_TO_SESSION supports BACK and BACK_OR_BOTH on new transports, rejects invalid directions and changes to existing channel roles
AUTH_SYS CB_NULL carries the offered timestamp, machine name, UID/GID and supplementary groups exactly
five-second probe timeout ignores late success; rebind recovers the path without recreating the session
losing the only callback transport sets CB_PATH_DOWN on a surviving forechannel connection
four backchannel offers preserve operation/concurrency counts and never increase buffer/RDMA limits; forechannel stays bounded
CREATE_SESSION retries preserve the original negotiated session; subsequent SEQUENCE/GETFH and explicit destruction work
SMB2.1/3.0/3.0.2/3.1.1 signed/encrypted asynchronous create/rename/delete, live ECHO, CANCEL and CLOSE cleanup
per-open first filter/watch-tree settings, FIFO completion and events buffered between requests
native host writes trigger recursive watches while nonrecursive watches ignore descendants
recursive watches stop observing moved-out subtrees and do not disclose queued outside names
SIZE filter ignores equal-length writes and reports actual growth
LAST_WRITE observes new-file writes even when native CREATE and WRITE are drained together
first per-open zero/short capacity persists, reopening restores capacity; NOTIFY_ENUM_DIR has no partial records; invalid-only filters stay pending and cancel cleanly
directory/list-access validation and persistent shared security descriptor changes generate SECURITY notifications
portable DOS attributes, creation-time and EA changes participate in native notification streams
initial CREATE metadata produces only ADDED; subsequent changes still produce MODIFIED
recursive descriptor exhaustion stays visibly overflowed across requests and releases all watches on close
delete-pending directories complete outstanding watches without waiting for last-handle deletion
TREE_DISCONNECT and LOGOFF finish pending notifications with NOTIFY_CLEANUP before releasing keys
policy revocation denies the pending poll, invalidates its old handle and permits a fresh exclusive read open without retained watch/sharing authority
NEGOTIATE respects requested credits, grants one when zero was requested and caps the window at 8192
bounded credit window tolerates delayed sequence IDs across 128 requests and still rejects replay
SMB-style wildcard bootstrap preserves SMB3.1.1 preauth/signing; SMB1-only, malformed and repeated probes rejected
0x300 negotiated signed login and operations; validate-negotiate for 3.0/3.0.2
0x300 encrypted AlSi/ExtA/MxAc/QFid contexts and selected EAs, Unicode IO, metadata, rename/delete, compound, srvsvc and 1 MiB SHA-256 stream
0x302 negotiated signed login and operations; validate-negotiate for 3.0/3.0.2
0x302 encrypted AlSi/ExtA/MxAc/QFid contexts and selected EAs, Unicode IO, metadata, rename/delete, compound, srvsvc and 1 MiB SHA-256 stream
0x311 negotiated signed login and operations; validate-negotiate for 3.0/3.0.2
0x311 encrypted AlSi/ExtA/MxAc/QFid contexts and selected EAs, Unicode IO, metadata, rename/delete, compound, srvsvc and 1 MiB SHA-256 stream
LOGOFF preserves the transport for a fresh encrypted session; short name queries return required length without disconnecting
default highest common dialect is 3.1.1; explicit CCM-only offer and encryption-required client work
AES-256-CCM/GCM-only offers use 32-byte directional keys, verified encrypted file I/O and same-handle NTLM renewal
leases and durable handles are not granted; durable reconnect explicitly unsupported; encrypted change notification cancels asynchronously; multichannel absent
SMB2.1 signed and SMB3.1.1 encrypted sessions share immediate data visibility and byte-range locks
absent encryption context is omitted from reply; no common cipher selects zero; CMAC/GMAC authenticated signed file I/O works without cipher fallback
cipher-free sessions reject unsigned commands and unnegotiated AES-GCM transforms even with correctly derived keys
repeated ignored NETNAME/transport/unknown contexts are accepted; missing mandatory preauthentication context returns INVALID_PARAMETER
unknown signing IDs select CMAC and unknown ciphers select zero; unsupported hash and malformed contexts fail without dialect fallback
independent AES-128/256 CCM/GCM transform decoding and replayed ciphertext rejected for each SMB3 dialect
AES-256-CCM/GCM reject modified tags, nonces, plaintext lengths, session IDs and ciphertext
tampered tags/ciphertext/AAD/session/size/nonce/signatures, unsigned requests, altered preauth chain, reused nonce and invalid validate-negotiate disconnect
fatal negotiate validation stops subsequent unrelated compound WRITE; exclusive-open cleanup barrier confirms unchanged file
SMB worker crash closes old sessions, recovers delete intent, preserves other workers and permits encrypted reconnect with new keys
